name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,306

clue.text: Pull dependant back (4)

indicators.note: 'back' as in going back the way you came: the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: a ward is a dependant in a guardian's care; read it back to front

annotation.surface: Someone hauls a person who relies on them back to safety.
annotation.walkthrough: A ward is a child or dependant legally under a guardian's care, a common crossword source for these four letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain verb synonym: horses draw a carriage, and a smoker draws on a pipe, both meaning pull.

clue.text: Tarnished tin made a shiny material (8)

indicators.note: a tarnished thing has been spoiled from its original state, so the letters are no longer in their original order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A dull metal is somehow turned into something glittering.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts tarnished and shiny, as if describing polishing; 'made a' belongs to the fodder rather than being a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the word is French for 'set with diamonds', and it names fabric or trim covered in glittering glass or sequins.

clue.text: Remove top of beam later (5)

indicators.note: in a down answer the word stands upright, so its top is its first letter, and that is what comes off

blocks.note: a rafter is a roof beam; take off its first letter R

annotation.surface: An instruction to a builder to take the upper part off a beam at a later stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Later' looks like a time for the building job; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adverbs: 'we'll talk about it after' and 'we'll talk about it later' say the same.

clue.text: Scholar’s account interrupted by media broadcast (8)

indicators.note: a speech interrupted by heckling has the heckling break into its middle, so the second part sits inside the first
seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered too

blocks.note: ACC is a standard abbreviation for account; it splits AC…C
MEDIA rearranged, placed between AC and C

annotation.surface: A scholar's version of events is cut short by a news broadcast.
annotation.walkthrough: '’s' stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun synonym: a university lecturer or researcher is called an academic, a scholar by profession.

clue.text: Cook at once sees hot snack (6,2,5)

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify them, so the letters are doctored into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: An instruction to get cooking straight away once someone spots a hot snack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot snack' reads as one phrase, but HOT is needed in the fodder, so the definition is just 'snack'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: grated cheese melted under the grill on a slice of toast is a classic British light bite.

clue.text: Five hundred pixies shortened burrow (5)

indicators.note: a word that is shortened has been cut down, and here it loses its final letter

blocks.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals
pixies are elves; ELVES without its last letter

annotation.surface: Five hundred small magical creatures, cut back in number, digging underground.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the pixies are doing the burrowing; 'burrow' is the verb that defines the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to delve was originally to dig with a spade, and to burrow is to dig into the ground.

clue.text: Main rock almost formed island (7)

indicators.note: almost the whole word means stopping one letter short of its end
clay that is formed is shaped into something new, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: anagram fodder
ROCK without its last letter

annotation.surface: A piece of geology: rock rising from the sea to make an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as 'the main', the open sea, which suits an island story; here it is just fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Minorca (Menorca) is one of the Balearic islands off Spain.

clue.text: Animal scoffing hot dog (4)

indicators.note: to scoff food is to gobble it up, so the first word swallows the letter that follows

blocks.note: a cow is an animal; it opens to take in the next letter
H = hot, as on a tap; goes inside COW

annotation.surface: A creature wolfing down a hot dog.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot dog' reads as the sausage in a bun; it splits into H and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the chow chow is a fluffy Chinese breed with a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: Fuddy-duddy in shape (6)

blocks.note: slang for an old-fashioned, conventional person
a four-sided figure with equal sides

annotation.surface: An old fogey who is keeping fit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In shape' reads as fit; the two words part and 'shape' becomes the second definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: 1950s slang for someone stuffy and out of touch, and the geometric figure with four equal sides.

clue.text: Old and short, quite wrinkled (7)

indicators.note: a word that is short of something is missing a bit, here its last letter
a wrinkled sheet has been creased out of its smooth order, so the letters are rumpled

blocks.note: AND without its last letter
QUITE rearranged

annotation.surface: Describing an elderly person: aged, small and rather wrinkly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a description of height, alongside 'old' and 'wrinkled'; it tells you to trim 'and'.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective synonym: antique furniture is old furniture, though the word usually implies value too.

clue.text: Jargon in advance written on back of manual (5)

indicators.note: text written on something is added on after it, so these letters follow
the back of a word is its end, so take its last letter

blocks.note: last letter of MANUAL
kept as it is
to go is to advance

annotation.surface: Technical terms printed on the back cover of an instruction manual, ahead of time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In advance' reads as 'beforehand'; the two words split, and 'in' is taken literally.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: lingo is informal for the special vocabulary of a trade or group, which is what jargon is.

clue.text: Vessel in amphora, or tankard (5)

indicators.note: the answer is literally in the words that follow, running across the gaps between them

blocks.note: amphorA OR TAnkard

annotation.surface: Where to find a drinking vessel: an ancient jar or a beer mug.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a pot, like the amphora and tankard that follow; it is a blood vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the body's main artery is the largest of the blood vessels.

clue.text: Fluff found in modest drink (6)

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so the first word goes into the second

blocks.note: shy = modest, retiring; it opens around the other part
to fluff a line is to make a mistake, to err; goes inside SHY

annotation.surface: Some lint discovered in an unassuming glass.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fluff' reads as lint; it is the verb to bungle.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a fortified wine from around Jerez in Spain is one kind of drink.

clue.text: Mushroom, advocaat and lemonade (8)

blocks.note: the verb: to grow very rapidly
a cocktail mixing Dutch egg liqueur with fizzy lemonade

annotation.surface: A list of odd ingredients: a fungus with egg liqueur and a fizzy drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' looks like a noun among the ingredients; it is the verb to grow fast. Advocaat is a Dutch egg-and-brandy liqueur, and the cocktail is a British Christmas favourite.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a problem that mushrooms grows like a ball rolled through snow, and the pub cocktail of advocaat topped with lemonade.

clue.text: Ultimate ban on rocky peak that’s flat (5,8)

indicators.note: something rocky is unsteady and wobbles about, so the letters shift out of place

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: A final ban on climbing a craggy summit that turns out to be level.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ultimate ban' tempts you to take the last letter of 'ban'; all three words are fodder, and 'rocky' belongs to the peak in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the mountain above Cape Town is famous for its level top, like a tabletop.

clue.text: State showing little interest in colour during time of prosperity (7)

indicators.note: something that happens during a period falls within it, so the colour sits inside the boom

blocks.note: a boom is a period of prosperity; it opens around the colour
red is a colour; goes inside BOOM

annotation.surface: A mood of indifference to colour in good economic times.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a long descriptive phrase, easy to mistake for part of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: the condition of feeling weary and uninterested is the noun for being bored.

clue.text: One, perhaps, is less sensitive (6)

blocks.note: one is an example, so 'perhaps' flags a definition by example
more lacking in feeling: a comparative adjective, not a noun

annotation.surface: A remark that a single person may feel less.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is two words spelt alike: the noun (NUM-ber) and the comparative of numb (NUMM-er).
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: one is a numeral, and something numb-er has lost more of its feeling.

clue.text: For example, some chicken run circled by wild animal (6)

indicators.note: a thing circled by another is ringed round by it, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a beast is a wild animal; it opens around the R
R = run, as in cricket scores; goes inside BEAST

annotation.surface: A chicken coop surrounded by a predator such as a fox.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chicken run' reads as the hen enclosure; it splits into the definition and R.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: white meat from the front of the bird is one cut of chicken you might buy.

clue.text: Protective garment worn regularly after month in spring (5)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so take every other letter
coming after the month, so these letters follow it

blocks.note: APR is the calendar abbreviation for April
second and fourth letters of wORN

annotation.surface: A garment put on often once April comes round.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Worn' reads as describing the garment; it is the source of the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a cloth tied over the front of the body to keep clothes clean is a protective garment.

clue.text: Bird beginning to make a raucous cry (5)

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of MAKE
kept as it is
a caw is a harsh cry, like a crow's

annotation.surface: A bird starting to squawk loudly.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole surface describes the bird itself, and 'beginning to make' reads as 'starting to make' rather than an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the large, loud, brightly coloured parrot of Central and South America is a bird.

clue.text: Strike beginning to affect country (5)

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw
first letter of AFFECT

annotation.surface: An industrial strike starting to hit a nation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strike' reads as a walkout; it is the informal verb to chin, to hit on the jaw.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the People's Republic in East Asia is a country.

clue.text: Learning, no end, for macho man (4)

indicators.note: with no end, the word has lost its final letter

blocks.note: study = learning; drop its last letter Y

annotation.surface: Endless education for a tough guy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No end' could mean 'a great deal'; here it trims one letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang sense: a stud is a stallion kept for breeding, and by extension a virile, macho man.

clue.text: Strange tour taking in back of terraced house (5)

indicators.note: strange means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put out of their ordinary order
a house taking in a lodger holds them inside, so the letter goes inside
the back of a word is its end, so take its last letter

blocks.note: TOUR rearranged, split around the next letter
last letter of TERRACED

annotation.surface: An odd guided walk that goes round the back of a row house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terraced house' reads as one thing, a house in a row; 'house' alone is the definition, meaning a royal dynasty.
annotation.definitionFit: A royal house is a dynasty, and the Tudors ruled England from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: Country song featured in musical (7)

blocks.note: the usual short name for the United States
a number sung by the Sharks girls in West Side Story

annotation.surface: A country-and-western number in a stage show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country song' reads as country music; 'Country' stands alone as the first definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the United States, and the Bernstein–Sondheim number from West Side Story.

clue.text: Revolutionary made it with no control (8)

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are turned into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder, joined 'with' the rest

annotation.surface: A rebel who succeeded without any leadership.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like the subject, a rebel; it is the anagram signal, and 'no control' reads as a phrase though 'control' stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: to hold sway over something, to have the upper hand over it, is to control it.

clue.text: Everything going past bat originally — for example, a bouncer (4)

indicators.note: a thing going past another ends up beyond it, so these letters come after
originally means at the start, so take the first letter

blocks.note: first letter of BAT
all = everything

annotation.surface: Everything flying past a cricket bat, like a short-pitched delivery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' reads as a nightclub doorman; in cricket it is a short delivery that rears up at the batter's head.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a bouncer is one kind of cricket delivery, and any bouncing sphere is also one.
